strategies.name: Sequential all-reduce with element-wise fusion
strategies.desc: Execute 8 all-reduce operations sequentially, fusing all local scale/divide operations between consecutive all-reduces into single vectorized kernels. 8 collective dispatches (one per all-reduce) with minimal local compute overhead. Represents the baseline with straightforward mapping of dependencies and maximum fusion of element-wise operations.

strategies.name: Pipelined two-stage all-reduce batching
strategies.desc: Group the 8 all-reduces into 2 batches of 4, overlapping local computation of batch i+1 with collective communication of batch i using asynchronous dispatch where possible. Still 8 collective dispatches but improved latency hiding through pipeline parallelism. Trades implementation complexity for reduced wall-clock time via overlap.

strategies.name: Hierarchical reduce-scatter then all-gather
strategies.desc: Replace each all-reduce with a reduce-scatter followed by all-gather pair (16 collectives total), allowing per-rank local computation on smaller chunks during the scatter phase. Doubles dispatch count but reduces per-dispatch payload size and enables rank-local scaling computation before gather. Favorable when local computation is the bottleneck.

strategies.name: Single-buffer in-place mutation chain
strategies.desc: Eliminate all intermediate buffer clones by carefully orchestrating in-place mutations with staging regions within the original tensor, using views and index manipulation. Still 8 all-reduce dispatches but removes memory allocation/copy overhead between stages. Minimizes memory footprint and bandwidth at cost of complex indexing logic.

strategies.name: Fused scale-reduce custom collective
strategies.desc:
Pre-compute all 8 iterations of scale coefficients locally, then implement a single custom collective operation that performs weighted reduction with iteration-dependent scaling factors in the reduction tree itself. Reduces to 1-2 collective dispatches by embedding computation into communication primitives. Maximum dispatch reduction but requires custom communication kernel implementation.
